challenge.method: Opened the fixed manual locator first and inspected both license sections. Independently opened the fixed release tag, pinned exception file, and revision 1 claim record. Compared the full release commit and instrument details, then tested whether the manual’s heading or file reference could establish either an unrestricted grant or applicability to a particular file.
challenge.results: The mixed-version challenge found no mismatch. The release tag and file pin use the same full commit, and the passage and file agree on the instrument’s identity. The GFDL merger reading fails because the manual places GFDL 1.3 in its separate documentation section. The unrestricted-grant reading fails because the instrument conditions its additional permission on Eligible Compilation Processes. The file-specific reading remains unsupported because the instrument requires a copyright-holder notice on the particular file, and the heading and COPYING.RUNTIME reference establish no such notice. limitations: The integrity pass covers the exact versioned locator and the observed passage’s consistency with the release lineage. Raw bytes of the rendered manual were unverified.
The SHA-256 field repeats the caller-supplied digest. The claim record was inspected through Web rendering, and its raw bytes were not hashed.
Support is limited to documentary identity in GCC 14.2.0. Any unrestricted grant, file-specific application, distribution authorization, source-byte identity, or crosswalk remains unsupported.
The active value is a registry proposal. Any approval or adoption of that lifecycle state remains unverified.

The claim SHA-256 was supplied as the public revision identifier. The operator checked the record bytes. The execution directly inspected the rendered versioned manual and makes no source or claim byte-capture assertion.
reasoning: Relevance passes because the manual’s code-license passage directly supplies each documentary fact in revision 1. Interpretation passes because that passage presents the exception as a distinct GPLv3 §7 additional permission, while the documentation section separately assigns GFDL 1.3 to the manual’s documentation category and explains the source-license treatment of documentation generated from source comments. Applicability passes for the GCC 14.2.0 passage and the exception’s stated edition. The claim record expressly describes active as a proposed index lifecycle state. Contradiction passes because the inspected evidence reveals no conflict with the scoped documentary assertion.
